extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties to PTAB inter partes review proceedings (petitioner and patent owner counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on whether and when a petitioner may offer a stipulation regarding parallel district-court proceedings (for the Fintiv discretionary denial analysis) and whether such a stipulation can serve as a basis for rehearing a decision denying institution of inter partes review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 4 (overlap between issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding." (Fintiv factor 4.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as part of the PTAB's discretionary-denial analysis under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a). Factor 4 assesses the degree to which issues in the petition overlap with issues that will be or are being litigated in a parallel district-court proceeding and can weigh against instituting an IPR if significant overlap exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for stipulations related to Fintiv factor 4
rubrics_metrics.description: "The only appropriate time for a petitioner to offer a stipulation related to the Fintiv factor 4 analysis is prior to the Board's decision of whether to institute review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stipulation offered for the first time after a decision denying institution (e.g., offered on rehearing) is not a proper basis for granting rehearing of the institution decision. Allowing late stipulations would frustrate the policy goals underlying the Fintiv analysis and could permit gamesmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance Memo policy on stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The PTAB will not discretionarily deny institution of an IPR or PGR in view of parallel district court litigation where a petitioner stipulates not to pursue in a parallel district court proceeding the same grounds as in the petition or any grounds that could have reasonably been raised in the petition." (Guidance Memo)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely stipulation (i.e., before the institution decision) can mitigate concerns about conflicting or duplicative proceedings and thus can influence the PTAB's exercise of discretion under Fintiv. The Memo is cited as Office policy (see Interim Procedure/Guidance Memo, June 21, 2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedential and panel treatment of stipulations (Sotera/Hulu)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior panels have found that stipulations can influence Fintiv factor 4 such that the factor weighs in favor of instituting trial (e.g., Sotera Wireless, Inc. v. Masimo Corp.; Hulu, LLC v. SITO Mobile R&D IP, LLC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel precedent predating the Guidance Memo has treated timely stipulations as relevant to the Fintiv analysis. Such precedent supports the view that stipulations offered before institution can reduce concerns about overlap and duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing standard under 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(c),(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rehearing addresses whether the Board "misapprehended or overlooked any matters" in the decision denying institution (37 C.F.R. § 42.71(c),(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rehearing request must point to misapprehension or overlooked matters; a new stipulation offered for the first time on rehearing does not ordinarily satisfy that standard because it was not presented to the panel before the institution decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain or justify late-filed stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board noted the petitioner "had not offered any explanation or justification as to why its stipulation is being offered so late in this proceeding."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party attempts to rely on a stipulation offered after the institution decision, the Board will expect an explanation for the late timing; absence of such justification supports denial of rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy purpose: mitigate conflicting decisions and duplicative efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidance Memo and Board decisions explain that the relevant policy goal is to "mitigate concerns of potentially conflicting decisions and duplicative efforts between the district court and the Board."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely stipulations help achieve this goal by reducing the risk of inconsistent outcomes and duplicative litigation; permitting post-denial stipulations undermines that policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review process for sua sponte review
rubrics_metrics.description: The "Interim process for Director review" provides for sua sponte Director review and explains that "the parties to the proceeding will be given notice" if Director review is initiated sua sponte.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director review can be initiated to address limited legal questions arising from PTAB decisions (here, whether a late stipulation can justify rehearing). The process and availability of sua sponte review are part of the procedural framework governing institution/rehearing disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of gamesmanship in timing of stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting a petitioner to wait to see if the Board denies institution under Fintiv, and then offer a stipulation for the first time on rehearing, "frustrates these goals and would open the door to gamesmanship."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should not delay stipulations until after institution decisions; doing so is viewed negatively and will likely be rejected as a basis for rehearing.
